items.title: Fix governance retrieval relevance scoring
items.body:
### Motivation

- The governance evaluation marked authoritative source documents as irrelevant due to legacy `source_document` values not being parsed or normalized into `relevant_document_ids`, causing retrieval metrics to be computed against mismatched IDs. 
- Retrieved chunk/document identifiers produced by the dispatcher and retriever used inconsistent shapes and path formats (Windows separators, `/app/data/raw/` prefixes, duplicate slashes, case differences) that prevented correct matching. 
- The scoring logic treated repeated chunks and document-level judgments inconsistently, resulting in incorrect Precision/Recall/MRR/NDCG values for cases with duplicate chunks from the same document.

### Description

- Map legacy `source_document` workbook field into `relevant_document_ids` while preserving the original `source_document` value in `source_fields` and supporting scalar, JSON, comma/semicolon/pipe/newline-delimited lists and N/A handling via improved `_list` parsing in `benchmark_loader.py`. 
- Add a shared `source_ids.py` module with `normalize_source_id`, `normalize_retrieved_chunk`, `retrieved_document_id`, and `retrieved_chunk_id` utilities to canonicalize IDs by converting backslashes to slashes, trimming whitespace, collapsing duplicate slashes, stripping runtime `raw` prefixes (`/app/data/raw/`, `data/raw/`, `./data/raw/`, `raw/`), and case-folding while preserving meaningful subpaths. 
- Normalize dispatcher outputs (`ExecutionDispatcher._normalize_chunks`) and update scoring (`retrieval_scores`) to: prefer chunk-level judgments when present, compare normalized document IDs otherwise, count duplicate relevant chunks at their returned ranks for Precision@5, MRR, and NDCG@5, and deduplicate when computing Recall@5 so each relevant document contributes at most once. 
- Add focused unit tests covering legacy `source_document` mapping, exact path matches, Windows-slash normalization, raw-prefix removal, duplicate retrieved chunks from one relevant document, multiple relevant documents, no relevant documents, document-level vs chunk-level judgments, and a GED-U-001 regression fixture; and update README to document normalization and duplicate-scoring conventions.

### Testing

- Bytecode/compile checks were run with `python -m compileall` over the modified evaluation modules and tests and succeeded. 
- Focused runtime assertions exercising `normalize_source_id` for Windows paths and all supported raw-data prefixes were executed and passed.

items.title: First-class conversation context + semantic-gated recall and stricter memory scopes
items.body:
### Motivation
- Prioritize recent conversation turns and transient session state over long-term memories for follow-up questions to avoid memory-system leakage and incorrect recalls.
- Keep short-term chat logs separate from durable memories and prevent raw chat observations or assistant-generated suggestions from being treated as durable facts.
- Reduce irrelevant memory recalls by gating on semantic relevance before applying recency/importance boosts.
- Provide a prompt contract so the LLM uses context in a predictable priority order and asks a clarification when references remain ambiguous.

### Description
- Add `ChatTurn` and `SessionState` dataclasses and persist recent conversation turns and session state in the store, with `append_conversation_turn`, `recent_conversation_turns`, `get_session_state`, and `update_session_state` implemented in `InMemoryStore`. 
- Extend `AgentChatRequest` with `conversation_id` and `recent_turns`, append user/assistant turns during chat, and assemble context in the prioritized order: current message, recent turns, active session state, relevant long-term memories, then general knowledge. 
- Introduce `MemoryScope` and `MemorySource` enums and attach `scope`/`source` metadata to `Memory` objects, and mark raw chat observations as `RAW_CHAT_LOG` so they are excluded from durable recall. 
- Add `message_has_unresolved_references` and logic to skip long-term recall when recent/session context sufficiently resolves follow-ups; add `recallable_long_term_memory` filter to prevent temporary/raw entries from being returned. 
- Add semantic gating (`SEMANTIC_RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD`) inside `hybrid_retrieval_score` so memories below threshold are rejected before recency/importance boosts. 
- Tighten memory extraction prompt to only extract user-authored claims (do not save assistant-generated assumptions) and update enqueue flow to avoid automatically persisting assistant-sourced assumptions. 
- Add prompt contract text and helper formatters (`format_recent_turns`, `format_session_state`) to ensure the LLM is instructed to use context in the requested priority and to avoid mentioning lack of saved memory. 
- Update store serialization/snapshots and memory serialization to include `scope`, `source`, and `expires_at`, and add session-state snapshots. 
- Add behavior-oriented regression tests that cover context-dependent follow-ups, prompt-contract coverage, semantic-gated recall, unrelated-memory suppression, and excluding raw chat logs from long-term recall (in `tests/test_api.py` and `tests/test_memory_os.py`).

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q` which executed the full test-suite and behavioral regressions, resulting in `19 passed, 1 skipped`.
- Ran `python -m compileall -q src` to validate Python compilation which completed successfully.
- New tests added exercise the new behavior: context-dependent follow-ups and prompt-contract checks in `tests/test_api.py` and unrelated-memory/raw-chat exclusions in `tests/test_memory_os.py`.

items.title: fix: widen sqlite-vec candidates before working-memory filters

sqlite-vec applies its KNN `k` limit before relational filters in the working-memory query. When the nearest unfiltered vectors belong to other sessions, applying session/scope filters can remove the entire initial neighborhood even though valid rows exist farther away. The empty result then incorrectly sends recall through the slower JSON-vector compatibility scan.

This change:

- starts with a bounded sqlite-vec candidate neighborhood;
- widens it geometrically until enough filtered rows are found or the vector table is exhausted;
- continues returning only the caller's requested result count; and
- adds a regression test with 600 closer vectors from another session ahead of one valid global row.

items.title: Fix Precision and Recall computation in retrieval evaluation
items.body:
Here is a concise English version of the PR description, suitable for a professional pull request.

---


This PR fixes a critical issue in the evaluation module where Precision and Recall were incorrectly computed. Previously, the code only calculated `Recall@1` (hit rate at rank 1) and misleadingly labeled a field as `"precision"` while actually assigning it the same value as `Recall@1`.

**Changes made:**

- Implemented **classic (global) Precision and Recall** using pooled aggregation of `TP`, `FP`, and `FN` counts across all queries:  
  - `Precision = Total_TP / (Total_TP + Total_FP)`  
  - `Recall = Total_TP / (Total_TP + Total_FN)`

- Removed the erroneous `"precision"` alias and replaced it with two distinct, accurate keys in the summary output:  
  - `"precision"` (global precision)  
  - `"recall"` (global recall)

- All other existing metrics (e.g., `false_answer_rate`, `multi_fact_evidence_coverage`, `failure_group_recall`) remain unchanged and their correctness has been verified.

**Impact:**

The evaluation report now provides trustworthy and interpretable Precision and Recall values, enabling a more accurate assessment of retrieval performance. This fix also decouples the metrics from any specific `K` value (Top‑K), making them valid regardless of how many documents are retrieved per query.

**Testing:**

Ran the evaluation script on the existing dataset and manually verified the new outputs against hand‑calculated values (e.g., Precision = 0.8, Recall ≈ 0.7567 on the sample data). All tests pass.

items.title: feat(r19): per-turn evidence labels on LoCoMo — and they refute yesterday's claim
items.body:
## What R19 does

`locomo_to_oracle.py` now emits per-turn `has_answer`, recovered from LoCoMo's `dia_id` / `evidence` fields. Matched **by dia_id, never by index** (empty-text turns are dropped, so positions do not correspond), with sessions **deep-copied per QA** (which turns are evidence differs per question). 1,438 questions, **2,140 evidence turns labelled**.

## The gate is code, not convention

The register made regeneration conditional on proving the R11 held-out sample had not moved. That is now `--verify`: regenerate with the same flags, strip `has_answer`, compare **serialized bytes**, exit non-zero without writing if they differ — reporting whether membership, order, or content moved.

```
GATE PASSED: locomo_full_answerable.json is byte-identical after stripping `has_answer`.
  1438 questions, 2140 evidence turns labelled, sample unmoved.
```

## The finding — it refutes #256's central claim

Rescoring the published baseline at **$0**. Same run, same retrieved keys, nothing re-executed:

| metric | session recall (published) | **evidence-turn recall (R19)** |
|---|---:|---:|
| micro | 95.06% | **59.86%** (1281/2140) |
| macro | 97.13% | **68.63%** |
| zero-evidence questions | 16 (1.11%) | **357 (24.86%)** |
| recall \| correct | 99.21% | **88.62%** |
| recall \| incorrect | 93.26% | **31.54%** |
| **difference** | **5.94pp** | **57.08pp** |

Dilution on LoCoMo is **20.6x** (44,162 evidence-session turns / 2,140 true evidence turns) — worse than LongMemEval's 12.2x.

**#256 concluded "retrieval is not the binding constraint." That is refuted.** A quarter of questions reach the actor with no evidence turn at all, and evidence-turn recall separates right from wrong answers by 57pp. Multi-session is the floor on both axes: 40.91% recall, 39.64% accuracy.

## Why the error happened

It is the R15 failure, committed in a document that *cites* R15. The doc correctly labelled session recall as diluted and then reasoned from it anyway. Labelling a diluted metric does not stop it being misread — making the real one computable does.

## Downstream

- **The retrieval-lever programme is not exhausted.** Every refuted lever was scored on session recall or the diluted key-recall; a lever fixing the 357 zero-evidence questions would have read as noise. Those nulls are weaker evidence than they were treated as.
- **G4 (term proximity) moves up** — admission-changing, so it can move zero-evidence questions.
- **The 65.02% accuracy is unaffected** and stays published as measured.

Correction banners applied to the result doc and `MEASURED_RECORD.md`; historical numbers left as written (Rule 5).

items.title: Look up macros from USDA instead of recalling them
items.body:
Ported onto `release-3.0.0`, preserving everything that branch already does: the Claude fallback, up-to-3-image scans, `MealImagePreprocessor`, the static-prefix/volatile-suffix prompt split, and `NutritionTargets`.

## Why

`release-3.0.0` already removed the chain-of-thought scratchpad and migrated to `thinkingLevel`. What remains is the part never addressed: the model still recalled USDA per-100 g composition **from memory**, did the arithmetic, and re-derived clinical thresholds on every request.

That's the wrong division of labour. Published evaluation of LLM nutrition estimation attributes the large majority of error to incorrect nutrient recall and [**none at all to arithmetic**](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.12843v1) — so the math-verification contract in the prompt was defending the one thing models reliably get right, while the actual failure mode went unguarded.

## What changed

Split by what each component is actually good at:

1. **Vision (paid)** identifies ingredients and estimates gram weights. Its response schema carries **no calorie or macro fields**, so it is structurally incapable of contributing a hallucinated nutrient value.
2. **`UsdaNutrientRepository`** resolves each ingredient against an embedded table (103 foods, 326 alias keys) → shared Mongo cache → live FoodData Central. Concurrently, so a ten-ingredient meal is one lookup deep rather than ten.
3. **`MacroCalculator` + `ClinicalRuleEngine`** compute totals, glycaemic load, budget and flags deterministically. Free, reproducible, testable. Rules like "sodium > 600 mg → HIGH" are comparisons, not reasoning.
4. **Narrative (paid, small)** explains the findings given the computed facts.

`FdcClient` owns the live tier: POST with `dataType` as a real array, `X-Api-Key` header rather than a query parameter, short timeouts, a conservative guard against the 1000/hour limit, and validation that rejects poor matches and implausible records. FDC will return a branded dessert for `"salt"` — accepting its top hit unconditionally would be worse than the model it replaces.

### Generation config still unaddressed on `release-3.0.0`

- `temperature` 0.1 → **1.0**. [Google's Gemini 3 guidance](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/gemini-3) warns values below 1.0 degrade mathematical and reasoning tasks. Determinism now comes from computing in Java, not from suppressing sampling.
- `media_resolution` **medium** — ~560 tokens/image vs ~1120 at the default high tier, which at 3 images is ~1700 input tokens.
- `responseSchema` on both stages, replacing prose schema and making fenced or truncated JSON impossible on the Gemini path.

### Fixes

Budget analysis now reads the **real daily log**. Previously consumed-today was never passed, so every meal was judged against an untouched day.

## Cost

Measured token profile falls from ~8.5k in / ~3.8k out to **~3.6k in / ~2.3k out** — roughly **−45% per uncached analysis** against current `release-3.0.0`, lower again with cache hits. Both paid stages sit behind a content-addressed cache keyed on image content and description, so a repeated meal costs nothing.

## Accuracy

Portion size dominates end-to-end error, so the extraction prompt spends its budget on reference-object guidance, and the confidence bracket is carried through to a **reported energy range** rather than a single figure the photograph cannot justify. Unmatched ingredients stay visible and flagged instead of vanishing into a confident-looking total.

Adds a MAPE eval harness. **It is a regression guard, not an independent measurement** — its references derive from the same table the code reads, and it says so. It buckets FDC-measured against regional IFCT-derived entries so the weaker path stays visible, and accepts photo cases with weighed reference values for genuine end-to-end ground truth.

## Deploy

Requires `USDA_FDC_API_KEY` ([free](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/api-key-signup.html)). Without it the live tier is skipped and unmatched ingredients are reported as unmatched, never guessed. A startup probe verifies the key and logs the result; `GET /api/v1/admin/nutrition/status` reports validity, quota and cache occupancy without exposing key material.

## Testing

52 nutrition tests, weighted toward refusals (bad matches, unit mix-ups, energy contradicting macros, 429s, no-key path). Full suite **138/139** — the one failure is the pre-existing `contextLoads`, which needs a Mongo URI and fails identically on `release-3.0.0`.

Not yet exercised against live Gemini or FDC with a real key; the startup probe exists so that first call announces itself rather than failing silently.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the memory-recall QA scenario reported success even when the recall turn produced no answer: its assertion rediscovered the acknowledgement from the earlier remember turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the outbound-message cursor immediately before asking the recall question, then require a matching assistant reply strictly after that cursor using the existing canonical QA waiter. The cursor counts outbound messages only, as required by the waiter's contract.

## User Impact

A broken memory-recall response can no longer appear as a passing QA scenario; genuine later recall answers continue to pass.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix regression runs the complete parsed scenario with the real QA bus and production outbound waiter; an earlier `Remembered ALPHA-7.` acknowledgement but no recall answer incorrectly passed.
- The paired positive control includes mixed inbound/outbound traffic and proves the correct outbound-only cursor is `1`, not the total-message count.
- Real Gateway + mock-provider execution passed the repaired `memory-recall` scenario; trusted Blacksmith Testbox aggregate passed **916 tests across 28 files**.
- Changes are limited to one QA scenario and one new focused regression; no runtime memory behavior, storage, configuration, or external provider contract changed.
- Independent structured review found no accepted actionable findings; Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30973152491

### Inspectable after-fix Gateway evidence

Observed on the trusted Blacksmith Testbox using a real ephemeral OpenClaw Gateway, the qa-channel transport, and a mock OpenAI model provider:

```text

provider: mock-openai
Gateway: real ephemeral Gateway
result: PASS
assertion: matching assistant recall reply occurs after the outbound cursor captured for the recall turn
```

The owner-path negative regression also confirms the old remember acknowledgement alone now fails; mixed inbound/outbound history preserves the outbound-only cursor.

items.title: feat(matching): canonicalization-aware organization-name scoring (canonical-jaccard)
items.body:
## Summary

Scoring track, change phase 1: organization names are now scored on the same canonical forms blocking already uses, closing the gap where blocking found pairs that scoring then threw away.

- **New `canonical-jaccard` similarity evaluator** (`Linkuity.Matching`): token-set Jaccard over canonicalized organization names (leading articles dropped, trailing legal suffixes stripped, ampersand initials collapsed — the same `OrganizationNameCanonicalizer` blocking uses, resolved per semantic type from the shared registration map). Two extra rules: a compressed-form equality check scores 1.0 when the canonical token sequences are identical modulo token boundaries (`AMAZON.COM` vs `AMAZON COM` → `AMAZONCOM`), the multiple-representation practice used by commercial ER engines; and fields whose semantic type has no registered canonicalizer fall back to plain raw-token Jaccard. Registered in both DI and the non-DI `MatchingDefaults` registry, with a parity test so the two sites can't drift.
- **Behavior change**: the built-in `organization` profile's `organization_name` switches `fuzzy` → `canonical-jaccard` (weight/roles unchanged; batch and durable; custom `*.profile.json` files unaffected). The company-resolution showcase adopts it too (`jaccard` → `canonical-jaccard`, thresholds unchanged).
- **Measured on the company-resolution showcase** (via `match scoring audit`, PR #35): 7 previously under-scored true pairs graduate to auto — Boeing (0.14 → 0.5714), Intel, Starbucks, Walt Disney, Ford, 3M, Texas Instruments. Scorecard: 59 → 52 golden records, pairwise recall 79.2% → 88.9% (F1 88.4% → 94.1%) at unchanged 100.0% precision and zero incorrect merges. Direct-edge audit recall 77.8% → 87.5% (63/72). The Disney-vs-Boeing false pair *drops* from the review band (0.3893) to 0.16 — canonicalization deflates false pairs for the same reason it fixes true ones. Blocking untouched: effective ceiling unchanged at 88.9%.
- **Docs/assets**: showcase README rewritten for the new scorecard (Boeing flips from "honest hard case" to resolved), evaluator documented in `how-matching-works.md` / `configuration.md` / `architecture.md`, CHANGELOG Added + Changed entries, demo.gif re-recorded and both Neo4j graph captures regenerated from a fresh export.

## Verification

- Full solution suite green at head (zero failures, all projects including Postgres/Testcontainers).
- All six measurement gates pass and were independently reproduced during review: audit precision 100.0% / recall 87.5%; showcase incorrect merges 0; left-separate exactly the three pure renames (verizon, att, meta); blocking ceiling 88.9% unchanged; Boeing explain `canonical-jaccard` sim 1.0000 → 0.5714 → auto; `CompanyResolutionDemoTests` passes against the re-pinned expectations.
- Measurement caught and fixed one real regression pre-merge: pure canonical Jaccard broke the Amazon pair (period-deletion fuses `AMAZON.COM` into one token, 0.87 → 0.29); the compressed-form equality rule restored it (0.8661, auto) with no other band changes.

## Known remaining misses (by design, tracked for future phases)

- `WALMART` vs `WAL MART STORES` (name-sim 0.0): needs adjacent-token-join variants — deliberately deferred; the cluster still unifies via other edges.
- verizon / att / meta: pure corporate renames, unreachable by name scoring — the identifier-profile (CIK/LEI) phase owns these.

items.title: Memorize: add immediate recall checks, timing, randomized order, and retry logic

### Motivation
- Improve the memorize (SRS) learning flow by introducing immediate retrieval checks, enforcing a short "instant recall" threshold, and offering randomized ordering to increase retrieval practice effectiveness.
- Make the session behavior more forgiving by reinserting missed pairs for near-term retry and provide clearer quiz feedback about slow responses.

### Description
- Replace the fixed quiz-frequency mechanism with an alternating recall direction and a timing threshold by adding `RECALL_TOO_SLOW_MS` and tracking `lastRevealAt` to require fast/instant recall for full credit.
- Add an optional randomize session order controlled by a new `memRandomizeOrder` checkbox stored in `localStorage`, and change `buildSessionQueue` to accept `randomizeOrder` and optionally shuffle the combined queue via `shuffleInPlace`.
- Introduce `insertQueueSoon` and `pendingRetry` so missed items are retried soon after an incorrect recall, and update session flow to use `pendingRetry` before pulling the next queued card.
- Change UI copy and behavior: the study action button label is now "Test me" and it triggers the recall quiz (`maybeRunMemQuiz`) rather than immediately marking as learned; quiz feedback distinguishes instant recall vs slow recall and correct answers now call `rateGood()` immediately.
- Remove the old `QUIZ_EVERY_N_CARDS` / `sinceQuiz` mechanism and wire up checkbox state persistence plus initialization from `localStorage`.

items.title: fix(recall): stop surfacing the agent's own assistant_response slices
items.body:
Closes #182.

## Problem
`thoth.self_action.assistant_response` was in `DEFAULT_RECALL_STREAMS`, so recall fed the agent its **own prior replies** back into context — circular, and actively harmful when those replies were wrong: a past incorrect diagnosis gets recalled with memory-authority (observed live 2026-06-17, where recall re-injected debunked findings as fact). It was also the dominant self-echo / rich-get-richer source.

## Fix
Remove it from the recall surface — **not** configurable, since there's no good reason to inject the agent's own replies. Recall now draws from `user_message.*` + the Summarizer's `summary` stream + the L1/L3/L4 headers (#177).

## Why this loses nothing
assistant_response slices belong in consolidation, not recall output:
- Still **written** — perception hook (`hermes_hooks.py`) + stream registration (`facade.py`) unchanged.
- Still **consumed**: the Summarizer (`summarizer.py`) distils them → `summary` stream; the Parser/Pattern-finder (`parser.py`) promote them → L1/L3. Both read by `metadata->>'session_id'`, independent of `DEFAULT_RECALL_STREAMS`.

Recall surfaces the **distilled** forms (summaries, entities, patterns), never the raw self-quotes.

## Tests
`assistant_response` excluded; `user_message.cli` + `summary` remain; no `self_state` streams. Full recall suite (95) passes.

items.title: fix(burn-train): correctly aggregate per-epoch metrics that require global statistics
items.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [ ] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Fixes #2758

Previously, metrics like Precision, Recall, and AUROC incorrectly assumed that global epoch-level scores could be computed by averaging individual batch-level metrics (weighted by sample count in `NumericMetricState`). This approach is biased for metrics requiring global statistics and sometimes entirely incorrect for metrics like AUROC and AUC-PR which cannot be meaningfully evaluated per-batch.

### Changes

- **Updated `Numeric` Trait:** Changed `value()` and `running_value()` to return `Option<NumericEntry>` (returning `None` for epoch-only metrics mid-epoch) and added `final_value()` to retrieve the computed metric at epoch completion.
- **Split `Metric` Execution:** Updated the `Metric` trait to decouple batch steps (`update`) from epoch-level finalization (`compute`). Updated `NumericMetricState` with `compute_update` and `compute_final` methods so that global aggregation is explicitly triggered at the end of each epoch (`end_epoch_train` in the event processor).
- **Added `ConfusionStatsState`:** Introduced a state structure that aggregates raw confusion matrix statistics (TP, FP, FN) across batches, enabling accurate global metric evaluation.
- **Updated `AurocMetric` & `AucPrMetric` via `PredictionAccumulatorState`:** Refactored `AurocMetric` to use `PredictionAccumulatorState` alongside `AucPrMetric`, accumulating raw prediction/target tensors during `update` and evaluating AUROC once over the full dataset during `compute`.

### Testing

## Summary

- Expand and normalize all 17 runtime prompt resource templates, covering intent, evidence rewrite, query enhancement, schema selection, feasibility, planning, SQL generation/repair, Python generation/analysis, reporting, JSON repair, chart selection, knowledge, and semantic-model inputs.
- Harden instruction/data/output boundaries and require exact structured-output contracts while preserving every runtime placeholder.

items.title: Fix pos_label not propagated to evaluate ROC/PR/calibration curves

labels.name: rn/bug-fix
labels.description: Mention under Bug Fixes in Changelogs.

items.body:
### Related Issues/PRs Closes #23991 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? `mlflow.evaluate(model_type="classifier")` computed the binary `precision_recall_auc` and the ROC / precision-recall / calibration **curve artifacts** against a hardcoded probability column (`y_probs[:, 1]`). `_validate_label_list` reorders `label_list` so `pos_label` is last, but the predicted-probability columns stay in the model's (sorted) class order. As a result, when `pos_label` is **not** the higher-sorted class: - `precision_recall_auc` is wrong (e.g. `0.32` instead of `~0.99` on a separable problem), - the ROC / precision-recall / calibration curve plots are produced for the wrong class. The scalar `roc_auc` happened to look correct because ROC AUC is symmetric under a positive/negative swap, which masked the bug. This PR: - captures the probability column matching `pos_label` (before `label_list` is reordered) and uses it when generating the binary ROC/PR curves in `classifier.py`, - selects the `pos_label` column in `plot_calibration_curve` instead of assuming column index 1, - makes the ROC AUC scalar respect `pos_label` by binarizing `y_true` against it. A targeted, localized fix was chosen over reordering `y_probs` globally because `plot_lift_curve` derives its own class order from `np.unique(y_true)`; a global reorder would have silently broken the lift curve. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] New unit/integration tests Added `test_evaluation_binary_classification_curve_auc_respects_pos_label`, which asserts `roc_auc` and `precision_recall_auc` from `mlflow.evaluate` match scikit-learn's values for the configured positive class. It fails on `master` for the non-default `pos_label` and passes with this change; the default `pos_label` is unaffected. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] Yes. Fixed a bug where `mlflow.evaluate` reported an incorrect `precision_recall_auc` and produced ROC / precision-recall / calibration curves for the wrong class when `pos_label` was set to the non-default class in binary classification. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/evaluation`: MLflow model evaluation features, evaluation metrics, and evaluation workflows #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/bug-fix` - A user-facing bug fix worth mentioning in the release notes #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release?

Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low.

items.title: Add LibreOffice pixel-parity benchmark
items.body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in, all-page Docxodus-versus-LibreOffice pixel-parity benchmark over 12 committed fixtures and 20 paired pages
- compare exact RGB, Lab ΔE76, block SSIM, tolerant ink F1, page geometry/count, and bounded ±2 px alignment
- emit portable JSON, SHA-256-addressed PNGs, and human-reviewable heatmaps outside the checkout
- add a scheduled/manual observational workflow, with an explicit strict mode for future gating
- document the first baseline, discrepancy clusters, false-positive controls, rejected hypotheses, and prioritized follow-up work
- fix paginated print handling of `w:webHidden` TOC results and Word's two-inch default footnote separator
- fix the one-sided-ink F1 edge case and pin all three fixes with independently generated regressions

## Why

The existing coverage is intentionally narrower: committed browser snapshots cover tab rendering, while the arcade/LibreOffice test compares one exported frame from each game. We need a repeatable document-wide diagnostic that renders every page through both engines and separates missing content, geometry, font substitution, and LibreOffice-specific behavior.

The initial baseline found 10 severe cases, 1 minor case, and 1 close case. That is expected and remains observational: the value of this PR is a reproducible discrepancy inventory and a trustworthy way to measure fixes, not a premature green gate.

## Safety and reproducibility

- every corpus path must be Git-tracked, a regular non-symlink file, and byte-identical to `HEAD:<path>`
- absolute, escaping, modified, untracked, or ignored fixtures are rejected before rendering
- generated DOCX, PDF, PNG, heatmap, and JSON artifacts must stay outside the repository in a new or empty directory
- tracked-change cases are accepted once into a temporary DOCX, then identical bytes are given to both renderers
- no masks are used
- the environment, source state, thresholds, relative artifact paths, and SHA-256 hashes are recorded

Two clean full passes produced identical normalized metrics and all 60 artifact hashes. No untracked harness/corpus content or generated render artifact is included in this commit.

## Root causes and impact

- `w:webHidden` is view-specific. Cached TOC leaders/page numbers belong in paginated Print layout even though they are hidden in Web layout.
- a percentage footnote separator drifted with text-area width; Word/LibreOffice use a fixed two-inch default. The change improved SSIM from 0.992055 to 0.992183 and tolerant ink F1 from 0.562434 to 0.565971.
- zero precision plus zero recall was incorrectly mapped to ink F1=1. It now maps to zero, correctly classifying blank chart output as severe.

The baseline also identifies chart fallback, tab-stop geometry, shape anchoring, footnote vertical placement, and a shared font-substitution contract as the next renderer priorities. Pagination/header-footer discrepancies already isolated in #372 are documented but not duplicated here.

## Validation

- `dotnet test Docxodus.Tests/Docxodus.Tests.csproj --no-restore --no-build --disable-build-servers -m:1`: 3,410 passed, 3 skipped
- focused generated C# regressions: 2 passed
- `npm run typecheck`: passed
- `npx playwright test visual-parity-metrics.spec.ts --project=chromium`: 5 passed
- full 12-case LibreOffice benchmark: passed in observational mode, 20 paired pages, 0 conversion errors
- repeat full benchmark: 60/60 PNG hashes and normalized metrics identical
- stale-output negative test: rejected the non-empty output directory before rendering
- `git diff --check`: passed

The full .NET run rewrote 47 spreadsheet fixtures as a test side effect; the pre/post audit caught them and restored those files to `HEAD`. They are not part of this PR.

items.title: feat: add canary context retention check for LLMDecide compaction
items.body:
## Summary

Add a canary-based context retention check to the LLMDecide `askLLM` flow. Each `askLLM` call appends an agent-visible `<agent:canary value="..."/>` message to `RecentMessages`. On the next call, the LLM is asked to recall its value. An incorrect answer indicates context degradation and **forces compaction** (overrides LLM decision).

## Motivation

LLMDecide compaction mode relied solely on token count heuristics — an indirect measure. Models can suffer "lost in the middle" degradation well before hitting context limits, or function perfectly even near limits depending on content distribution. The canary directly tests whether the LLM can attend to mid-context information.

## Cache-Friendly Design

The canary is **appended** (never inserted mid-list), so the provider prefix-cache for earlier messages is unaffected. The canary naturally sinks to the "lost in the middle" zone as tool call/result messages accumulate. After each `askLLM` call, old canaries are cleaned and a new one is appended for the next round.

| `pkg/compact/canary.go` | **New** — `AppendCanary`, `FindCanaryValue`, `RemoveAllCanaries`, `generateCanaryValue` |

items.title: Normalize query/doc ID matching in evaluation to fix zero/incorrect precision and recall
items.body:
The retrieval pipeline was returning valid hits, but evaluation often computed zero/incorrect precision and recall due to mismatched identifiers between retrieved results and ground-truth entries. The fix aligns query and document identity handling across evaluation paths so relevance comparisons are performed on canonical values.

- **Root cause addressed: canonicalization gap in evaluation**
  - Added a shared `EvaluationNormalizer` to normalize:
    - query strings (trim, quote removal, whitespace collapse, lowercase)
    - document IDs (path separator normalization, `./` cleanup, canonical tail form, lowercase)
  - This removes false negatives caused by equivalent-but-different string forms.

- **Ground-truth consistency**
  - Updated `GroundTruth` to store normalized query keys and normalized relevant document IDs.
  - Updated lookup (`getRelevantDocs`) to normalize incoming query text before map access.

- **Precision/recall computation alignment**
  - Updated `EvaluationService` and `Evaluator` to compare normalized retrieved IDs vs normalized relevant IDs.
  - Centralized relevant-hit counting in shared normalization-aware logic, including controlled filename fallback when one side is unqualified.

- **Net effect**
  - Precision and recall now reflect actual overlap between retrieved results and judgments instead of string-format artifacts.

```java
// before: direct string comparison could miss equivalent IDs
relevantDocs.contains(result.getDocumentId());

// now: both sides compared in normalized canonical form
String docId = EvaluationNormalizer.normalizeDocId(result.getDocumentId());
long relevantRetrieved = EvaluationNormalizer.countRelevantRetrieved(
    retrievedNormalizedDocs,
    relevantNormalizedDocs
);
```

items.title: Align flashcard system with SM-2 specification and session length flow
items.body:
## Removed deviations
- removed non-spec `user_progress` fields introduced in earlier Phase 2 work: `correct`, `last_reviewed_at`, `review_interval_days`, and `next_due_at`
- removed the ad-hoc interval-doubling persistence path that was not using the product data model
- replaced due selection based on `next_due_at` with spec-based `due_date` ordering

## New schema changes
- added a cleanup migration that drops non-spec review fields and reasserts the spec fields/defaults on `user_progress`
- regenerated `types/database.ts` so `user_progress` matches the spec-backed schema again

## SM-2 rules implemented
Binary correct/incorrect recall now updates `user_progress` using the spec-aligned SM-2 variant:
- correct recall:
  - `repetitions += 1`
  - first correct => `interval = 1`
  - second correct => `interval = 6`
  - later correct => `interval = previous_interval * easiness_factor` (rounded to an integer)
  - `easiness_factor += 0.1`
- incorrect recall:
  - `repetitions = 0`
  - `interval = 1`
  - `easiness_factor -= 0.1`, bounded to a minimum of `1.3`
- always:
  - `due_date = now + interval days`
  - `last_reviewed = now`
  - `review_count += 1`

## Priority ordering behaviour
For authenticated users, server-side selection now follows the product priority order:
1. Due cards (`due_date <= today`)
2. New cards (no `user_progress` row)
3. Backlog cards (seen before, but not due yet)

If the user is not logged in, the page keeps the simple `limit(10)` fallback and does not attempt SM-2 scheduling.

## Session length behaviour
- `/flashcards` now starts with a session length selector
- supported lengths: `1 minute`, `3 minutes`, `5 minutes`, and `unlimited`
- queue size uses a simple 6-seconds-per-card heuristic:
  - 1 minute => about 10 cards
  - 3 minutes => about 30 cards
  - 5 minutes => about 50 cards
  - unlimited => no cap
- the session ends automatically when the queue is exhausted and shows the summary screen
- on session completion, authenticated users update `user_stats.last_session_date`

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`

## Summary

Recall could end before a file save was done. A test could then remove the temp folder too soon. The late save failed because the folder was gone.

Remnic now keeps a list of saves made by recall. Stop waits for those saves before it closes runtime tools. Recall itself does not wait. Failed saves still stay best effort.

The drain covers the last recall state, handle history, eval shadow data, direct answer notes, and access counts. The affected tests now stop Remnic before they delete temp folders.

items.body:
## What

An agentic workflow that labels open PRs with which development phases they affect — restore, build, bootstrap, compiler output, design-time, test tooling, or agent configuration. Runs hourly. Text-only — reads diffs via GitHub API, never checks out or builds PR code.

**Not** a code quality check or merge-readiness signal. Detects changes in design/build/agentic-time behavior.

## State machine

| What you see | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No label | Not yet scanned |
| `AI-Tooling-Check-Bypassed` | Trusted author or non-fork — skipped |
| `AI-Tooling-Check-Scanned-Clean` | Diff analyzed, nothing interesting |
| `⚠️ Affects-*` | Diff analyzed, PR touches that phase |

Labels re-evaluated on new commits (head SHA check).

## Categories

**Generic (.NET):** Build-Infra, Restore, Agent-Config, Scope-Review-Needed
**Repo-specific (edit per repo):** Bootstrap, Compiler-Output, Design-Time, Test-Tooling

Categories use principle-based descriptions — the agent applies judgment, not a file list. Catches novel extension points a checklist would miss.

## Safety

- No shell, no checkout, no filesystem — only `pull_requests` MCP read access
- Output: max 10 labels from fixed allowlist + max 1 comment (replaces previous)
- Network: `defaults` + `github` egress only

items.title: Hero Demo #1: cross-source company resolution (SEC EDGAR + GLEIF)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds Linkuity's first **showcase** (`showcases/company-resolution/`) — a polished, self-contained demo that resolves **49 real US companies** across two independent public systems, **SEC EDGAR** and **GLEIF**, that share *no* common identifier. Resolution runs on company **name + address only**; the CIK↔LEI crosswalk is held out and used purely to validate.

Also introduces the top-level `showcases/` directory (distinct from `samples/`: samples are small teaching datasets for learning matching config; showcases are end-to-end demos on real public data) and a `showcases/README.md` catalog.

## Result (machine-verified, reproducible)

- 107 source records → **60 golden records**
- **38 / 49 companies correctly unified**, **0 incorrect merges**
- **Precision 100.0% · Recall 80.6% · F1 89.2%**

Zero false merges is the hard gate — enforced by both a PowerShell scorecard (`validate/Test-Resolution.ps1`) and a C# regression test (`CompanyResolutionDemoTests`), which pins the golden count and asserts no cluster mixes two companies.

## Why it's convincing (and honest)

- **No cheat key.** SEC keys on CIK, GLEIF on LEI — they don't overlap, so resolution must work from a fuzzy name and a postal address. Identifiers never enter `run/companies.csv` or the profile; they live only in `validate/ground-truth.csv`.
- **Real data, projected verbatim.** Every name/address comes byte-for-byte from the live APIs (e.g. a malformed `98027-` ZIP and lowercase `c/o` survive untouched). The only "duplicates" are genuine SEC `formerNames` records.
- **Failures shown, not hidden.** The 11 split companies are reported with reasons — e.g. GLEIF `THE BOEING COMPANY` vs SEC `BOEING CO` never become match candidates, and true rebrands (Bell Atlantic→Verizon) can't bridge on name alone.

## Notable decisions

- **Dropped Chevron:** its NYSE parent has no LEI in GLEIF at all, so pairing it would mix a parent SEC record with a subsidiary GLEIF record. 49 honest pairs over 50 with an asterisk.
- **GLEIF headquarters address, not legal address:** GLEIF's *legal* address is frequently a shared Delaware registered-agent address (noise that even caused a Boeing+Disney false merge and capped unification at 24/49). Projecting the real *headquarters* address lifted it to 38/49 and eliminated the false-merge ceiling. This is disclosed transparently in the showcase README.

## What's included

`showcases/company-resolution/`:
- `acquire/Get-Sources.ps1` + `prepare/Build-Input.ps1` — live SEC+GLEIF fetch → committed input (offline-runnable; `-Refresh` re-pulls)
- `run/` — committed `companies.csv`, tuned `company.profile.json` + `company.merge.json`, pinned `expectations.json`
- `validate/` — scorecard + held-out `ground-truth.csv`
- `run-demo.ps1` — one command: run → validate (`-Neo4j` also emits a graph export)
- `assets/` — mermaid pipeline diagram, golden-org graph, VHS recording tape
- Flagship `README.md` with verified numbers and side-by-side match examples

Repo wiring: `showcases/README.md` catalog, a single link line from the root README, `.gitignore` for generated output/cache.

## Scope / safety

- **Config-only** — the sole C# added is the one regression test (`CompanyResolutionDemoTests`). No engine/production code changed.
- Full suite green (**498 tests**). Clean-clone `./run-demo.ps1` runs offline and reproduces 60/0/100%.
- Data licensing: GLEIF is CC0; SEC EDGAR is US-government public domain (attributed in the README).

items.title: fix(search): restore official DeepSearchQA grading
items.body:
## DSQA currently collapses item-level grading into binary accuracy

The current grader uses a compact noncanonical prompt and asks Gemini for one `all_expected_answers_found` boolean. That removes the per-answer decisions required by the DeepSearchQA paper, gives partial answers no continuous score, and makes strict Fully Correct accuracy the only headline result. The official dataset card warns that changing the judge prompt can produce statistically significant score differences.

## TL;DR

Restore the versioned Kaggle/paper prompt and nested correctness-detail verdict, call Gemini 2.5 Flash without a response schema as the official starter does, calculate per-question precision/recall/F1 plus all four categories, and use macro F1 as DSQA's primary score. Strict `accuracy` remains the Fully Correct rate.

## What Changed?

- Sends the official grader prompt to `google/gemini-2.5-flash` with no explicit temperature or structured-output override.
- Parses bare or `json`-fenced official verdicts and validates every detail value and excessive answer.
- Computes per-question precision, recall, F1, Fully Correct, Fully Incorrect, Partially Correct, and Correct with Extraneous Answers.
- Mean-reduces epochs per question, macro-averages across questions, and exposes macro `f1_score` through the existing primary-score hook.
- Keeps malformed non-skipped grades at zero and excludes skipped infrastructure failures, matching existing harness aggregation boundaries.
- Updates the exported judge-prompt provenance hash and documents the metric contract.
- Makes structured output optional in the shared judge helper; every existing judge that supplies a schema remains unchanged.

## Why?

The paper ranks systems by macro per-question F1. Preserving only the final strict predicate cannot distinguish a nearly complete answer from a fully wrong answer and cannot reproduce the published methodology. Dynamic correctness-detail keys also cannot be represented faithfully by the existing strict fixed schema, so DSQA follows the official free-form JSON call while retaining fail-closed parsing.

## Validation

Local validation passed:

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run check` (pre-existing warning-level findings only)
- `bun run typecheck` (291 files, zero diagnostics)
- `bun test` (1,173 passed)
- `bun run build`

GitHub `validate`, CodeQL, and JavaScript/TypeScript analysis all pass. The mirrored search-benchmarks implementation also completed a paid 10-task DSQA run through the official free-form judge path with 10/10 valid verdicts and no skips or parse failures.

## Reviewer Focus

- Confirm the prompt text and hash match the pinned Kaggle starter.
- Confirm macro F1 is the mean of per-question F1 values, not pooled F1 or F1 of macro precision/recall.
- Confirm empty correctness-detail maps fail closed rather than becoming vacuously Fully Correct.
- Confirm omitting `text.format` is DSQA-only and leaves structured judges unchanged.

items.title: RVW02-WS08: decouple calibrator (off by default) + deduped-union round-1
items.body:
Decouples the LLM calibrator from the round-1 review path (re-scoped WS08, `for #669`).

## What changed

- **Calibrator is now OPTIONAL and OFF by default.** `run_fanout_review(calibrator=None)` (the default, threaded all the way down from an unset Roster `calibrator`) no longer means "use the shipped judge" — it means the judge is OFF.
- **Default round-1 = the mechanically-deduped union.** New pure `dedup_union` groups the pass union by `(file, line, normalized-claim)`, keeps the most-severe member as the canonical (ties → lowest union id), and merges the rest as `duplicate_of` entries that ride the record but never double-post. The canonical posts with its OWN pass-assigned severity — no LLM judge, no model run in the default path.
- **`route_calibrated` is shared by both paths** (nit cap, duplicates-never-post, derived status), so the off path routes identically to the on path minus the judge.
- **Calibrator kept warm, dormant** (concept, config, hooks, and the F2 reproduction-based floor all wired): a reviewer opts it back on by configuring a `calibrator` inline-table in its Roster entry.
- New `review.deduped` event (the off-path twin of `review.calibrated`).
- ADR-0045 amended with the decouple decision + rationale; config/roster docstrings corrected (`calibrator` unset = off, not default-on).

## Why

The WS05/F2 A/B baseline (#638, #665) measured the LLM calibrator **net-negative on round-1 major recall**: on app#391 the passes surfaced the true `Editor.svelte` major and the calibrator *refuted it incorrectly*, dragging fan-out recall (0/3) below the single-pass baseline (1/3). The fan-out is the bet with outside evidence; the calibrator was an unproven precision layer bolted on. Decoupling restores the union's app-G1 major → recall back to ≥ single-pass, while the calibrator stays re-enablable for later, independent tuning (#665).

## Context

- **Approach:** `calibrator: CalibratorConfig | None` already flowed end-to-end; making `None` mean OFF (rather than falling back to `DEFAULT_CALIBRATOR`) is the whole opt-in switch — no new sentinel, no adapter. `dedup_union` reuses the existing `CalibratedFinding` / `duplicate_of` machinery so `route_calibrated`, the attestation, the round record, and the posting path are all untouched below the branch.
- **Dedup is deliberately conservative:** it merges only same-location same-normalized-claim candidates. Semantic overlap of differently-worded findings is the LLM judge's job and is NOT attempted mechanically — a mechanical merge must never fuse two genuinely distinct findings. Nothing is ever *dropped* on the off path (mechanical dedup only merges); the nit cap can still suppress via `route_calibrated`.
- **Out of scope (do not "fix" here):** the calibrator's verification-reasoning bug / app-G1 wrong-refutation (#665, deferred with the dormant calibrator); large-PR detection depth where core-G1/G3 never surface (#666); WS06/WS07. Union recall ties single-pass at 1/3 *because of #666* — it does not regress.
- **Not run here:** the `ws05-arm-union` re-baseline replays run coordinator-side against this branch (per the brief + #663 — no backgrounded replays from an implementer Run).
- **Self-check vs governing docs:** ADR-0045 (updated in this diff), the WS05 report (#638), and the full data record + re-scope on #669. The decision boundaries in the brief (keep the calibrator, mechanical dedup, fan-out stays invisible below the reviewer boundary) are all honored — prstate/funnel/reconcile are untouched.
- **Verify:** full `pixi run test` green; lint clean via hooks. Added off-path integration tests + `dedup_union` unit tests; opted the judge-path tests into an explicit `calibrator=_CAL`.

items.title: fix(search): contain invalid benchmark responses
items.body:
## Invalid responses cross the wrong failure boundaries

Two search-benchmark outcomes currently inherit generic infrastructure-error behavior:

- A completed response with blank text becomes a retryable `503`. After retries, the harness records it as `Skipped`, removing the question from accuracy and primary-score denominators.
- DeepSearchQA intentionally uses the official free-form judge contract. One malformed verdict becomes a status-less `ModelError`, which is systemic and fails the harness invocation instead of only that sample.

In the internal Temporal worker, the first path can persist a completed aggregate over only the model's nonblank answers. The second path retries the affected chunk activity and can leave a partial run after retry exhaustion.

## TL;DR

Keep bounded retries for completed blank responses, but after exhaustion return the final completed response to normal scoring so all four search suites count it as incorrect. Keep DSQA on the official unstructured judge request, but use the existing parse-fallback contract to emit a zero-credit sample with parse evidence instead of failing the chunk.

## What changed?

### Completed blank responses remain benchmark outcomes

- Retry blank completed responses with the existing schedule.
- Recover only the exact synthetic blank error after the retry budget; later provider or incomplete-response errors remain failures.
- Preserve usage and generation time from every completed blank attempt plus any eventual valid response.
- Let BrowseComp, HLE, DSQA, and WideSearch skip unnecessary judge calls and score exhausted blanks as `Incorrect`.

### DSQA parse failures fail closed per sample

- Keep `jsonSchema` absent, preserving the official Kaggle/paper grader request.
- Supply a DSQA-specific fallback verdict through `parseFailureFallback`.
- Produce precision/recall/F1 `0`, `fully_incorrect: 1`, and primary-score weight `1`.
- Attach the parser error to the existing `judge_runs` trajectory so Parquet and Mission Control retain diagnostic evidence.
- Preserve judge usage/cost on the fallback path.

## Why?

`Skipped` is appropriate for exhausted provider capacity or incomplete transport results, but not for a response that completed and supplied no answer. Likewise, judge-format nondeterminism should not invalidate unrelated samples in the same worker chunk. Both changes keep failure policy at the narrow benchmark-specific boundary instead of weakening global `ModelError` classification.

## Compatibility and sequencing

No exported package path, benchmark config, Temporal payload, or OpenAPI schema changes. Successful DSQA trajectories are unchanged; failed parses add only an optional `error` field.

After merge:

1. Update the pinned benchmark-harness commit in `search-benchmarks`.
2. Re-sync the vendored subtree in `openrouter-web#33074`.
3. Deploy `gcp-bench-worker` only after that updated subtree lands.

No paid inference calls were made.

items.title: fix(facts): make retirement work + stop extractor ingesting noise (#325, #326)
items.body:
## Summary

Two defects let incorrect facts accumulate permanently and dominate recall.

### #326 — `supersede_fact` / `mark_superseded` were no-ops
The handler called `markSuperseded(id, null)`, which set `superseded_by = NULL` — exactly what recall treats as "active" — so "retired" facts kept serving. Retirement-without-a-successor was structurally impossible: invariant I5b requires `superseded_by` to reference a real fact, and self-supersede is guarded.

**Fix:** nullable `retired_at` column (`022_facts_retired_at` sqlite + pg) · `FactStore.retire()` on both adapters + the pg tx queue (sets `retired_at`, drops the embedding so semantic recall can't surface it) · recall excludes retired facts (keyword via SQL `AND retired_at IS NULL`, semantic via embedding deletion) · `includeSuperseded` / `getHistory` still surface them for audit · `supersedeFactHandler` now calls `retire()`.

### #325 — the extractor ingested its own recall block + null-result values
The classifier saw NLM's injected "Possibly-relevant prior sessions" pointer block as transcript content and extracted facts from it (a feedback loop), and stored process non-answers ("…result not provided", "did not run") as high-confidence facts.

**Fix:** `stripInjectedContext` removes the pointer block (header → `NLM tools:` footer) before classification, wired into `ClassifierBox.classify` — the single seam ingest/scheduler/backfill funnel through · `isNonAnswerValue` gate in `coerceFacts` deterministically drops null-answer values (the local classifier isn't trusted to self-police).

## Tests
+21 (retire contract ×5, handler ×5, retire→recall e2e ×1, strip ×6, classifier-box wiring ×1, value gate ×3). Full suite **1106 pass / 0 fail**; `build:server` + `typecheck` clean.

items.title: Wire HNSW into search, and complete the M2 documentation
items.body:
Closes the last open drift from M2: the index was built and tested, but vector_search always ran the exact scan because nothing owned the decision of when a cached graph is still good enough.

IndexCache owns it now, in one place rather than spread through the search path. It lives in AppState so one graph is shared across requests -- a rebuild is O(n log n) and doing it per query would cost more than the scan it replaces.

The policy and why each part is what it is:

- Index above 2000 vectors. Below that, scanning beats building AND walking a graph. Conservative default, not a measured optimum -- there are no benchmarks yet.
- Detect staleness with a per-collection generation counter, bumped on every vector write and delete. Counting would be O(n) per query, and a count cannot see a delete-then-add that leaves the total unchanged.
- Rebuild a stale graph after 30s. Rebuilding per write would rebuild continuously under load.
- Fall back to the exact scan if a build fails. An optimisation that cannot be built must not fail a query.

The first draft of access() took a caller-supplied vector count, which would have forced an O(n) count on every query -- the exact scan it exists to avoid. It counts internally now and caches the too-small verdict under the same generation-and-staleness rule as the graph itself.

WHY BOUNDED STALENESS IS SAFE HERE, when a stale secondary index is not: the graph supplies candidates only. Scores are recomputed from the stored vector, and a candidate whose record is gone is skipped. So a deleted document cannot surface and an updated one scores by its new vector; the only effect is that a document written in the last 30s may not be found yet. Bounded recall loss on new data, never incorrect data. That asymmetry is the entire justification for caching rather than maintaining the index transactionally, and it is written up as ADR-022. A test pins both paths to the same nearest neighbour with a byte-identical score.

FIXED, a live availability bug found while verifying the documented quick start against a running server: a shadow collection is an ordinary collection, so any client with write access could insert a document into one, and anything that did not decode as a VectorRecord made for_each_vector fail -- turning every subsequent search on that collection into a 500. One insert could brick search. Undecodable documents are now skipped and logged at warn.

FOUND, not fixed: byo is the default embedding provider and has no ingest route, so search on a byo collection returns nothing, always. The only working path is writing raw records into the shadow collection using internal serde shapes -- an implementation detail acting as a public contract. Recorded as an open drift with a proposed endpoint rather than designed unilaterally, because it is a public API surface.

Documentation: new docs/vectors.md; ADR-021/022/023; roadmap M2 marked complete with a planned-versus-built table including the two crate-level surprises (hnswlib-rs needs nightly, anndists::DistDot asserts on non-unit vectors); testing updated with a sixth load-bearing invariant; docs/handoff.md for picking the work back up. The README was still claiming secondary indexes were unimplemented, and its vector config example did not deserialize -- both config payloads in the docs are now verified verbatim against a live server.

## What & why

`recall` synthesizes its answer with a local LLM, so it can be wrong. This adds a `force` flag (default `false`) to the MCP `recall` tool. When `force` is falsy the tool rejects the call with a warning that recall is experimental and may return an incorrect answer, instructing the caller to retry with `force=true` (and to prefer `search`/`browse` for verbatim memories).

items.title: Compute the links union in SQL to close the lost-update race (#38)
items.body:
Fixes #38.

`link()` read the links list into Python, appended, and wrote it back. That `SELECT` ran outside any transaction — `sqlite3` only opens one on the first DML — so two concurrent `link()` calls touching the same memory could both read the same "before" list, and whichever `UPDATE` committed last silently overwrote the other's addition.

Each `UPDATE` now unions the new id in a **single self-contained statement**, so it reads the row's true current value at write time under the row lock and there is no window to lose. This is the second option the issue recommended, and the same `json_each`/`json_group_array` pattern `remember()`'s ON CONFLICT upsert already uses for the identical problem (#47/#59) — worth having both sites use one idiom.

## Verification

Reproduced the issue's own scenario — 4 memories, all 6 pairwise links fired from simultaneous threads on separate connections, so every node is touched by 3 of the 6 calls (worst case):

```
OLD (read-modify-write)                NEW (SQL union)
  memory 1: links=[4]     LOST           memory 1: links=[2,3,4]  OK
  memory 2: links=[1]     LOST           memory 2: links=[1,3,4]  OK
  memory 3: links=[1]     LOST           memory 3: links=[1,2,4]  OK
  memory 4: links=[1]     LOST           memory 4: links=[1,2,3]  OK
  edges: 6/6 explicit                    edges: 6/6 explicit
```

Exactly matching the issue's report of "1 of 3" surviving per node.

That reproduction is now a test — and **it fails when the old read-modify-write is reintroduced**, so it detects the bug rather than passing vacuously. Two smaller tests cover idempotence (linking twice, and in reverse, doesn't duplicate) and that the union merges with links an earlier `remember()` set rather than replacing them.

The test also asserts the `edges` table stays 6/6. As the issue notes, `edges` was always correct here — but `memories.links` is the only source of truth if `edges` were ever rebuilt from scratch, which is why the silent incorrectness was worth fixing even though it wasn't observable through `recall`.

**235 passed**, 2 skipped on both mcp majors; ruff clean.

items.title: fix(hermit): session-mgr report filename is invariant (#418)
items.body:
## Summary

The archiving model (session-mgr, downgradable to haiku in deployment) could improvise a dated `S-NNN-REPORT-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.md` stub when the canonical `S-NNN-REPORT.md` already existed, because the archive steps never stated what to do in that case. The stub bypasses strict-glob consumers (catalog injection, reflect, weekly-review) but surfaces in `/recall`'s broad `globDirRecursive` scan, potentially injecting incorrect claims into future sessions.

## Changes

- `agents/session-mgr.md`: canonical-filename invariant added in three locations — On Session Close step 5 (leading sub-bullet), On Task Complete step 5 (one-sentence note), and `## Rules` (standalone bullet for partial-read resilience). In all cases: always `${session_id}-REPORT.md`; if it already exists, overwrite in place; never create a suffixed second file.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `[Unreleased] ### Fixed` entry.

## Root cause / investigation

No code anywhere generates a timestamped report name — `daily-auto-close` (the issue's proposed fix location) writes no files; session-mgr is deterministic to the canonical name. The improvisation happens at the LLM level when the canonical file already exists and no instruction covers that case. Fix is prompt hardening at the writer.

## Test plan

- `bun test` in `plugins/claude-code-hermit/` — 1115 pass, 0 fail (doc-only change to an agent file, all contract tests green).
- One-time operator hygiene on live hermits: `ls .claude-code-hermit/sessions/S-*-REPORT-*.md` and delete any existing stray stubs.

Closes #418

items.title: fix(memory): stop a turn recalling the question it is answering

labels.name: risk: medium
labels.description: Auto risk: src/** or dependency/config changes.

items.body:
## Problem

Auto-save writes each user message to memory **before** recall runs, so by the
time the `[Memory context]` block is built the store already holds a verbatim
copy of the question being asked.

That copy is worthless as context — the same text sits in the prompt directly
below the block — and it is actively harmful. Being a perfect lexical match it
takes the top rank, and scores are normalised **relative to the best hit**, so a
single self-echo pushes every real fact under `min_relevance_score`.

The effect, measured on a live store with the same query and the same config,
differing only in `auto_save`:

| `auto_save` | keys reaching the prompt |
|---|---|
| `true` | `["user_msg_ddbebf17-…"]` — one entry, its own question |
| `false` | `["long_note","release_cadence","daily_deploy","deploy_window","roadmap_note"]` |

With the default settings, curated memory was effectively never reaching the
model. Clearing the `conversation` category did not help — the next turn
re-writes its own entry before recalling.

This was invisible until #417 made injection visible.

## Change

`build_memory_context` drops entries whose content **is** the message being
answered, then re-ranks the survivors.

Two details carry the fix, and each is separately mutation-tested:

- **Dropped before the score threshold, not after.** By the time the threshold
  runs, the echo has already defined the ranking everything else is measured
  against — filtering it later changes nothing.
- **Re-ranked after the drop**, so "relative to the best hit" means the best
  *usable* hit.

One place, three callers: the agent, the channel dispatcher and the CLI loop
share this builder.

An entry that merely *mentions* the topic is untouched — only a verbatim echo
is dropped, matched after collapsing whitespace so a re-wrapped copy still
compares equal.

## Known limit

Asking the same question verbatim N times leaves N stored echoes. Past the
small over-fetch margin the usable page shrinks by one per extra echo — at four
identical turns the block went from five entries to four. Widening the recall on
*every* turn to buy headroom for verbatim repeats costs more than the case is
worth; what is lost is the weakest-ranked entries, and nothing incorrect enters
the prompt. Documented on the constant.

## Not changed

`recall_layered` puts conversation-scoped hits ahead of shared memory, and both
tiers share one entry budget. That balance is a design decision, not a defect,
and it is left alone here.

## Validation

- `cargo test --lib memory:: / agent:: / channels::` and `--test agent_e2e`,
  `--test memory_comparison` — 1311 passed.
- **Mutation-tested both halves**: skipping the re-rank fails 2 tests; moving
  the drop after the threshold fails the same 2.
- Strict delta gate — clean.
- Live, `auto_save = true`, gateway and TUI:

```
↺ recalled 5 memories: long_note, release_cadence, daily_deploy, +2 more
```

  Stable across repeated turns (2, 3, 4).

## Risk / rollback

**This changes what every turn sends the model** — that is the point, but it is
the blast radius. One file, one function, no config or schema change. Revert the
commit.
